title: Father Conmee thought of the souls of black and brown and yellow men
html_source: Father Conmee sees a black man on the street and that sparks his to thoughts about “the souls of black and brown and yellow men”. He is referring to people in Asia, Africa and North America, clearly, but what is significant about this line is the fact that he thinks of the “souls” of these people. His thoughts are framed in terms of salvation: since he represents the church’s ideology, it is not surprising that his own thoughts and perceptions are overlayed with the concerns and vernacular of his religion. This becomes more evident throughout the episode.
